trends.trend: Capital commitments: how many dollars and gigawatts are already contracted through ~2031
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Trillions of dollars of signed purchase and lease commitments set how much AI capacity exists by 2028-2031, and therefore how cheap and ubiquitous AI services, agents and automation become at work and at home.

trends.trend: Chip, memory and packaging supply chain as the binding bottleneck (incl. export controls)
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Fabs, HBM memory and lithography tools ramp on multi-year schedules; shortages show up as rationed AI access, dearer phones/PCs/consoles and geopolitics around Taiwan and export licences.

trends.trend: Frontier-lab economics and AI capability trajectory (revenue run-rates, time horizons, AGI timing)
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: How fast models improve and how much revenue labs earn decides which jobs are automated when, what software costs, and whether 'AGI announced' is a 2027 or a 2031 headline.

trends.trend: Financing structure and fragility: leases, guarantees, vendor finance, debt costs, bubble risk
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: The build-out is financed with long leases, vendor guarantees and high-coupon debt; if revenue lags, the unwind hits pensions, bond funds, local tax bases and jobs, and if it holds, the same structures concentrate wealth.

trends.trend: Where it lands: gigawatt campuses, power, local siting fights and moratoria
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: Gigawatt campuses land in specific counties (Ohio, Texas, Louisiana, Tennessee), bringing construction booms, gas turbines, grid strain, higher power bills and ballot fights over moratoria.
